# Error codes and what to do

The wizard explains every failure with a row of `install/deep32-wizard-errors.tsv`. The full screen shows the row as "What it means" and "What to do". This file holds two parts of that table: the exit statuses and the VM guide's codes. Look up any other code in the table itself, as below.

## Look up a code

Run one of these from the repository folder. Put the exact code or a short exact piece of the line in place of CODE.

```sh
grep -n -F -- 'CODE' install/deep32-wizard-errors.tsv
```

```powershell
Select-String -SimpleMatch -Path install\deep32-wizard-errors.tsv -Pattern 'CODE'
```

Each row has six fields separated by a TAB: kind (exit, code or text), key, os (any, linux, windows or macos), source (the tool that prints it), meaning, and fix. The fix is up to five steps separated by " | "; text in backticks is a command. Use the row whose os matches the machine; otherwise the "any" row. A "text" row's key is a pattern for a whole output line, so search for a short exact piece of the line. Tell the person the meaning and the steps word for word.

## Exit statuses

The key is TOOL:STATUS. The full screen shows them under "What the tools said", for example "deep32-get exit 10".

**setup:0**: The setup step finished.

1. On this machine, do any [you] lines above; they are the steps only you can do

**setup:1**: Setup stopped at a [fail] line, or it found [fix] lines it could not fix itself.

1. Read the [fail] and [fix] lines above; the wizard explains each one
2. Do the steps on the machine each line names
3. Run the wizard again

**setup:64**: Setup was started with an argument it does not know.

1. On this machine, run the setup with --help to see its roles (check, forge, workstation, headend) and options
2. Run the wizard again without the extra argument

**get:0**: The download or install step finished and its files are verified.

1. On this machine, follow the Next: line the step printed, if any

**get:1**: The download tool stopped on a trust or input problem: a signature, checksum, option or local file check failed.

1. Read the message above this line; the wizard explains it
2. Do not use files that did not pass verification
3. Run the wizard again; finished downloads are kept

**get:2**: A download helper refused its arguments, or the verified disc 3 media could not be joined.

1. Read the message above this line; the wizard explains it
2. Run the wizard again; finished downloads are kept
3. If it happens again, keep the log the wizard names and report it; do not delete Deep32 files by hand

**get:3**: The selected disc is not in this release yet; the signed release lists it as pending.

1. In a browser, check the release page (github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/releases) for that disc
2. Run the wizard again once the disc is published there

**get:10**: A prerequisite or storage action needs you before the step can go on; that stage installed nothing.

1. Read the lines above: each names what is missing and gives a Next: action
2. Do those actions on this machine, and restart it if a line asks for a restart
3. Run the wizard again

**get:11**: The disc 3 loader was interrupted or reached its deadline, so the install stage needs you.

1. On the GPU host, check the GPU pack with the status and recovery commands in src/gpu-pack/PACK.md
2. Run the wizard again with the same choices; the install resumes from its recorded state

**get:130**: The step was interrupted with Ctrl+C.

1. Run the wizard again; verified parts are kept and the download resumes

**get:143**: The step was stopped from outside, for example by a shutdown or a service manager.

1. Run the wizard again; verified parts are kept and the download resumes

**inventory:0**: The prerequisite check passed for this machine.

1. On this machine, go on with the next step the wizard shows

**inventory:1**: The prerequisite checker hit an error, for example a missing or unreadable matrix or prerequisites file.

1. On this machine, check that the Deep32 folder is a complete source kit (install/matrix.json and install/prerequisites.json are there)
2. Get a fresh copy of the source kit if files are missing
3. Run the wizard again

**inventory:2**: The prerequisite checker was given arguments it does not accept.

1. On this machine, run the checker with --help to see its options
2. Run the wizard again
3. If it happens again, keep the log the wizard names and report it; do not delete Deep32 files by hand

**inventory:3**: The checker refused: gaming mode is on or its state file cannot be read, or the bench was asked for on Windows.

1. On this machine, turn gaming mode off if it is on
2. Run the wizard again

**inventory:10**: One or more prerequisites need your action, or a restart is still pending.

1. Read each line of the form id=missing and the Next: line under it; the wizard explains each id
2. Do those actions on this machine, and restart it if a line asks
3. Run the wizard again

**forge:1**: The Forge installer failed on its input or on a host operation.

1. Read the Forge message above this line; the wizard explains it
2. On the GPU host, keep the same verified disc 3 media attached and the same data folder
3. Run the wizard again; the installer retries the same action

**forge:2**: The Forge installer's host check refused this machine, or the installer was given arguments it does not accept.

1. Read the Forge message above this line; the wizard explains it
2. Fix the item it names on the GPU host
3. Run the wizard again

**forge:3**: An interrupted converter job left a recovery record, so no other job can run yet.

1. On the GPU host, as administrator or root, run recover with forms/forge_jobs.py (src/gpu-pack/PACK.md, Forge conversion and index jobs)
2. Then run the job again

**forge:4**: The operator GPU hold is on, so the Forge will not start a converter or builder job.

1. On the GPU host, release the GPU hold (the status/gpu-hold file in the Forge data folder) once the GPU is free for Deep32
2. Then run the job again

**forge:10**: The Forge installer needs an action from you; its message names it.

1. Read the Forge message above this line; the wizard explains it
2. Do that action on the GPU host
3. Run the wizard again

**forge:11**: The Forge installation changed while it was being checked, another lifecycle operation is running, or a deadline expired.

1. On the GPU host, wait until any other Forge operation has finished
2. Run the wizard again; it retries the same action

**forge:130**: A Forge job was interrupted with Ctrl+C.

1. On the GPU host, run recover with forms/forge_jobs.py if the job left a recovery record (src/gpu-pack/PACK.md)
2. Then run the job again

**forge:143**: A Forge job was stopped from outside, for example by a shutdown.

1. On the GPU host, run recover with forms/forge_jobs.py if the job left a recovery record (src/gpu-pack/PACK.md)
2. Then run the job again

**connect:0**: Connect finished.

1. On the agent PC, start the agent with the launcher Connect printed

**connect:1**: Connect refused, or it could not read or write its local files; its message names the cause.

1. Read the message above this line; the wizard explains it
2. Do what it names on the agent PC
3. Run the wizard again

**connect:2**: Connect was given arguments it does not accept.

1. On the agent PC, check the arguments: --agent claude, codex or both and --workstation https://NAME.TAILNET.ts.net/mcp (PowerShell: -Agent and -Workstation)
2. Run the wizard again

**connect:10**: Connect needs something from you first, such as installing or signing in to the agent, approving a merge, or an interactive window.

1. Read the message above this line; the wizard explains it
2. Do what it names on the agent PC
3. Run the wizard again

**connect:11**: The pairing code expired or the pairing timed out.

1. On the Workstation, open Pairing and choose Headend to get a new ten-character code
2. On the agent PC, run the wizard again and type the new code within five minutes

**connect:12**: Pairing is locked after three failed windows in thirty minutes; it unlocks after fifteen minutes.

1. Wait fifteen minutes; do not delete the lockout files
2. On the Workstation, open Pairing and choose Headend for a new code
3. On the agent PC, run the wizard again and type the code

**connect:13**: The Workstation refused the enrolment, or the gateway failed a check after pairing.

1. Read the message above this line; the wizard explains it
2. On the Workstation, open Pairing and choose Headend for a new window
3. Run the wizard again

**connect:14**: The agent PC could not reach the Workstation gateway over the tailnet (address, TLS, redirect or no answer).

1. On the agent PC, check that Tailscale is signed in to the same tailnet as the Workstation (run `tailscale status`)
2. On the Workstation, check that publication runs: `/usr/local/d32/sbin/d32-publish status`
3. Use the exact https://.../mcp address publication printed
4. Run the wizard again

**relay:0**: The relay action finished.

1. On this PC, follow the lines the relay printed

**relay:10**: The relay action did not complete; it printed a relay check code or operation code.

1. Read the code in the lines above; the wizard explains it
2. Keep the relay folder as it is; Connect keeps it for review
3. Run the same relay command again after the fix

## VM guide codes

A VM step shows "Result: ERROR CODE". The hypervisor file may hold a fix of its own for the same code; use that one first.

**send-no-disc2**: The verified disc 2 is not in the download folder next to the Deep32 folder on this machine, so there is nothing to send.

1. On this machine, run the wizard and choose Workstation host; it downloads and verifies disc 2 into that folder
2. Then run Send disc 2 again

**send-no-tailscale**: Tailscale is not installed on this machine, so it cannot send disc 2 over your tailnet.

1. On this machine, in a terminal, run: `curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh|sh`
2. Sign in with `sudo tailscale up` and the account your Workstation uses
3. Run Send disc 2 again

**send-no-tailscale** (windows): Tailscale is not installed on this PC, so it cannot send disc 2 over your tailnet.

1. On this PC, in PowerShell, run: `winget install --exact --id Tailscale.Tailscale --source winget`
2. Sign in to Tailscale with the account your Workstation uses
3. Open a new PowerShell window as administrator and run Send disc 2 again

**send-signed-out**: Tailscale on this machine is not running or not signed in.

1. On this machine, in a terminal, run: `sudo tailscale up`
2. Open the address it prints in any browser and sign in with the account your Workstation uses
3. Run Send disc 2 again

**send-signed-out** (windows): Tailscale on this PC is not running or not signed in.

1. On this PC, in PowerShell, run: `tailscale up`
2. Sign in with the account your Workstation uses in the browser window it opens
3. Run Send disc 2 again

**send-needs-root** (linux): On Linux, Tailscale serves a file only for root or for its operator user.

1. In the Deep32 folder on this machine, run the send as root: `sudo bash install/deep32-wizard.sh --send-disc2`
2. Or make your user the Tailscale operator once: `sudo tailscale set --operator=$USER`, then run Send disc 2 again

**send-needs-root** (windows): On Windows, Tailscale serves a file only from an Administrator console.

1. On this PC, open PowerShell as administrator (Start, type PowerShell, right-click, Run as administrator)
2. In the Deep32 folder, run: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File install\deep32-wizard.ps1 -SendDisc2`

**send-needs-root**: Tailscale serves a file only for an administrator of this machine.

1. In the Deep32 folder on this machine, run the send as root: `sudo bash install/deep32-wizard.sh --send-disc2`

**send-serve-refused**: Tailscale refused to serve disc 2, or stopped serving it. Serve needs MagicDNS and HTTPS certificates on in your tailnet.

1. Read what Tailscale said above
2. In a browser on any device, open the Tailscale admin console DNS page (login.tailscale.com/admin/dns) and turn on MagicDNS and HTTPS Certificates
3. On this machine, run `tailscale status` and check that it is connected
4. Run Send disc 2 again

**send-port-busy**: Port 9447, the port Send disc 2 uses, is taken on this machine: by another Send disc 2, another Tailscale serve or another program.

1. If another wizard window is sending disc 2, use that one, or press Enter there to stop it
2. Otherwise, on this machine run `tailscale serve status` and stop what uses port 9447
3. Run Send disc 2 again

**send-self-check**: This machine did not answer at its own tailnet address with the whole disc 2, so the Workstation could not fetch it either.

1. Read what the check said above
2. On this machine, check that no other program uses port 9447 and that `tailscale serve status` shows the disc 2 path while it sends
3. Run Send disc 2 again

**VM_FIRMWARE_UEFI**: The VM boots with UEFI. The Workstation installs and boots with BIOS (legacy) firmware.

1. In your hypervisor, set the VM's firmware to BIOS (legacy)
2. Check the step again

**VM_GENERATION**: The Hyper-V VM is Generation 2, which boots with UEFI only. The Workstation needs Generation 1 (BIOS).

1. Create the VM again as Generation 1, with the step's New-VM line
2. Check the step again

**VM_DISPLAY_VIRTIO**: The VM has a virtio-gpu display. The Workstation desktop has only been tested with a standard VGA display.

1. In your hypervisor, set the VM's display to standard VGA
2. Check the step again

**VM_CPU_LOW**: The VM has fewer than 4 vCPUs. The Workstation needs at least 4; 6 are recommended.

1. In your hypervisor, give the VM 6 vCPUs (at least 4)
2. Check the step again

**VM_MEMORY_LOW**: The VM has less than 8192 MiB of memory. The Workstation needs at least 8 GB; 12 GB is recommended.

1. In your hypervisor, give the VM 12288 MiB of memory (at least 8192)
2. Check the step again

**VM_DISK_SMALL**: The VM's largest disk is smaller than 200 GB. The guided install needs an empty target disk of at least 200 GB.

1. In your hypervisor, give the VM an empty disk of at least 200 GB
2. Check the step again

**VM_INSTALLER_MISSING**: The VM has no installer disk: the small disk made from disc 1 is not attached.

1. Attach the installer copy as the VM's first disk, as the step says
2. Check the step again

**VM_BOOT_ORDER**: The VM boots from the wrong disk. For the install it boots the installer; after the install it boots the 200 GB disk.

1. Set the boot order, or detach the installer after the install, as the step says
2. Check the step again

**VM_CDROM_MISSING**: The VM has no CD/DVD drive with disc 2 in it.

1. Attach disc 2 as a CD/DVD drive, as the step says
2. Check the step again

**VM_NIC_MODEL**: The VM's network card is a model this recipe does not use. OpenBSD runs Intel PRO/1000 cards (em), VirtIO (vio) and VMXNET3 (vmx).

1. In your hypervisor, set the network card the step names
2. Check the step again

**VM_OS_TYPE**: The VM's Proxmox OS type is not other, the value the tested VM uses.

1. On the node, set ostype other with qm set, as the step says
2. Check the step again

**VM_CPU_TYPE**: The VM's Proxmox CPU type is not host, the value the tested VM uses.

1. On the node, set the CPU type host with qm set, as the step says
2. Check the step again

**VM_DISK_CONTROLLER**: The VM's SCSI controller is not VirtIO SCSI single, the value the tested VM uses.

1. On the node, with the VM stopped, set scsihw virtio-scsi-single with qm set
2. Check the step again

**VM_CHIPSET**: The VirtualBox VM's chipset is not PIIX3.

1. With the VM shut down, set its chipset to PIIX3
2. Check the step again

**VM_NOT_FOUND**: The wizard could not read this VM: no VM there has this name, ID or file, or the query was refused.

1. Check the VM's name, ID or .vmx path on the settings screen (Esc goes back to it)
2. Run the wizard in a session allowed to query the hypervisor (Hyper-V: PowerShell as administrator)
3. Check the step again

**NET_HOSTONLY**: The VM is on a host-only, internal or private network, or has no network. The Workstation needs outbound internet for its Tailscale sign-in.

1. Connect the VM to a bridged or a NAT network, as the network screen says
2. Check the step again

**KIT_MISSING**: No verified disc 1 with deep32-get's VM folder was found. The guide reads the image's path, size and SHA-256 from that folder's recipe.json.

1. In the Deep32 folder, make the VM folder: `bash src/release-tools/deep32-get.sh disc1 --to ./deep32-downloads --prepare-vm --hypervisor kvm`
2. Run the VM guide again; for another download folder, add --kit FOLDER

**KIT_MISSING** (windows): No verified disc 1 with deep32-get's VM folder was found. The guide reads the image's path, size and SHA-256 from that folder's recipe.json.

1. In PowerShell, in the Deep32 folder: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File src\release-tools\deep32-get.ps1 disc1 --to .\deep32-downloads --prepare-vm --hypervisor hyper-v`
2. Run the VM guide again; for another download folder, add -Kit FOLDER

**KIT_COPY_FAILED**: A file in the kit folder could not be written, or the copy is smaller than the image.

1. Check that the kit folder is writable and has room for another copy of disc 1
2. Delete the half-written installer.vdi or installer.vmdk
3. Check the step again

**PVE_TLS_MISMATCH**: The node's certificate is not the one you compared, or its fingerprint did not match. The wizard sent no token to it.

1. On the node, read the fingerprint again with `pvenode cert info`
2. If it changed and nobody changed it, stop and find out why
3. Check the step again

**PVE_TOKEN_DENIED**: The Proxmox API refused the token: the secret is wrong, or the token has no PVEAuditor role on this VM.

1. On the node, give the token the PVEAuditor role on /vms/VMID with pveum acl modify (the settings screen shows the command)
2. Check the step again and type the secret

**PVE_UNREACHABLE**: The wizard could not reach the Proxmox API on port 8006 of the node, or the API answered with an error.

1. Check the node address on the settings screen (Esc goes back to it)
2. From this PC, open https://ADDRESS:8006 in a browser
3. Check the step again

**TS_NOT_HERE**: This PC is not signed in to your tailnet, so the wizard cannot see the Workstation join.

1. Confirm the join in the Tailscale admin console
2. Or sign this PC in to Tailscale and check the step again

**TS_PEER_MISSING**: No new machine with the Workstation's name is online on your tailnet yet.

1. On the Workstation's console, finish the sign-in with the address it shows
2. If the sign-in stalls, give the VM's network another DNS server: DNSSEC through some routers' DNS fails
3. Check the step again
